problem: The CDC release path requires fresh independent SPEC and code-quality reviewers, but the available GitHub Copilot review-request route accepted the request without materializing any requested reviewer, review, review thread, or review comment. The same failure mode had already occurred on an earlier CDC 2.11.2 review attempt.

hypotheses.statement: The request failed because the Copilot reviewer login used by the caller was incorrect.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare the requested reviewer login against current GitHub documentation for REST review requests.
hypotheses.observed_result: Current GitHub documentation explicitly identifies copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] as the REST reviewer identity, which is the exact value requested.

hypotheses.statement: The request failed because the pull request was draft and therefore not reviewable.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Issue the request on a non-draft full-diff pull request and read back reviewer/review surfaces.
hypotheses.observed_result: PR #77 was created non-draft; the request still produced no requested reviewer, review submission, review thread, or review comment.

hypotheses.statement: The currently available independent-review channel is unavailable or nonfunctional for this repository/account/tool route, so a successful request call is not evidence that a reviewer was actually assigned or ran.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Request the documented Copilot reviewer on a non-draft exact-head full-diff PR, then independently read requested-reviewer, review, review-thread, and comment surfaces; compare with the earlier independent-review attempt.
hypotheses.observed_result: All four readback surfaces remained empty after the request, and the earlier PR #69 attempt recorded the same no-materialization outcome. The execution channel therefore cannot currently supply the required independent reviewer identity.

correction: Add an explicit independent-review backend reconciliation/failover contract: a review request is only submission evidence, never review evidence. After requesting a reviewer, read back a concrete reviewer/review identity and durable review result. If the requested backend does not materialize, classify it unavailable/no-op, avoid unchanged retries, route to another authorized independent reviewer backend when available, or persist a blocker with the exact candidate and next review action.
defense_in_depth: Bind review evidence to exact source commit, package tree, metadata head, review stage, reviewer identity, and review artifact; keep SPEC and code-quality stages ordered; retain no-op backend observations so later invocations do not repeatedly spend the same failed strategy.
invariant: A required independent review stage can advance only from a concrete fresh reviewer identity plus a durable review result bound to the exact candidate; accepted review requests, empty reviewer surfaces, or unchanged retries never satisfy or bypass the gate.
